title: A Range iterator's knownSize overflows when last - start does not fit in Int, so iterator.toVector, to(ArrayBuffer), toList and mkString silently drop elements
oracle: knownSize is -1 or the number of remaining elements; BigInt model of the range
generator: wave4/harness/collections3/RangeDiff.scala: start, end and step drawn from the Int extremes with a step that divides the span into a few elements; iterator knownSize compared with the model's count
seed: seed 1, 60 s run; case number not recorded
detail: RangeIterator.knownSize (src/library/scala/collection/immutable/Range.scala, class RangeIterator) is (lastElement - _next) / step + 1 in Int arithmetic. When the range spans more than Int.MaxValue the subtraction wraps: (Int.MinValue to Int.MaxValue by Int.MaxValue) has 3 elements and its iterator reports 1; (-1073741826 until Int.MaxValue by 715827883) has 5 and reports 0. Builders and conversions size themselves from knownSize: iterator.toVector and iterator.to(ArrayBuffer) return 1 element of 3 without an error, and with a reported 0 iterator.toList is Nil and iterator.map(f).mkString is empty while hasNext is true. Range.length itself is right, so only code that goes through the iterator is affected. It needs a range wider than 2^31 with a large step, which is rare in ordinary code.
fix_sketch: Compute the remaining count in Long, ((lastElement.toLong - _next) / step + 1), and return it when it fits in Int, else -1. No compatibility cost.
